note: b497 DESIGNER RULING (final authority) - the last new-player death loop. A fresh character has 10 max HP and takes 4.94 damage per goblin kill; the death sheet teaches “unlock Auto-Eat”; Auto-Eat is priced in Bounty Marks; the cheapest Mark is a tier-1 cull of 80-120 kills. The tutorial pointed at a currency the first session could not reach. The AWAY half was the P0: simulateSpan BREAKS on the first death, so a new player who left a fight running overnight was credited THIRTY SECONDS of a twelve-hour night - the idle pillar was off by default for every new account, behind a 15-Mark toll. THE RULING: every new character starts owning `auto_eat` (tier I, fixed <25% threshold). `auto_eat_2` (100 Marks, the SETTABLE threshold) is untouched - the sink survives, the entry tax does not. HOW: the SAME player_progress row hr_trait_buy__ungated §8 writes (kind='flag', key='trait:auto_eat', period_key='' - the exact shape hr_auto_eat_tier reads and the unlock guard polices), then the switch set DIRECTLY on the row the bootstrap just inserted, with the clamp DERIVED: auto_eat_pct = hr_auto_eat_max_pct(hr_auto_eat_tier(v_uid, v_slot)), the exact expression hr_set_auto_eat evaluates, so neither the ceiling (25) nor the tier (1) is restated. Order is load-bearing - the flag row first, because the clamp reads the tier. ⚠ IT DOES NOT CALL hr_set_auto_eat, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE SUBTLETY OF THE FILE. hr_set_auto_eat remains the single writer for every LATER change, but it also bumps `version` and writes a set_auto_eat player_ledger row - both correct in isolation, and both read by 2026-08-17-cutover-import.sql §(e) as the DEFINITION of “this character has already played” (version > 0, or any non-create_character ledger row dated at/after created_at). hr_import_apply CALLS hr_create_character, so routing the switch through it makes the CUTOVER CEREMONY REFUSE EVERY PLAYER. Measured on a full PGlite replay, not reasoned about: the first draft did call it and turned all six of tests/cutover-import.mjs's snapshots red; restoring version=0 afterwards fixed half of it and the ledger row still failed the other half. §2 asserts BOTH halves (the switch is set; hr_set_auto_eat is NOT called here) so it cannot be quietly tidied back. §1b IS A NECESSARY CONSEQUENCE, NOT AN OPPORTUNISTIC EDIT: with one bootstrap-written progress row, hr_import_apply's progress verify - which compared the envelope's permanent-row count against `v_n_prog`, a counter of rows THE PLAN wrote - is off by exactly one for every player (`verify_mismatch: progress 11 <> 10`, measured). Patched, anchored exactly-once and CR-tolerant, to compare ENVELOPE vs TABLE - the shape the inventory and farm arms either side of it already use. ⚠⚠ THAT IS A WEAKENING, CORRECTED 2026-08-30 (Security review): an earlier version of this note called the replacement equivalent, and the reviewer disproved it. The table holds bootstrap+plan and hr_state_of returns bootstrap+plan (an import plan writes no ev:kill_monster / ev:loot keys, so none of its projection filters bite), so the new test is B+P <> B+P - a TAUTOLOGY that cannot fail. THIS FILE THEREFORE REMOVES player_progress IMPORT VERIFICATION. Skills, inventory and equipment are still verified value-by-value and a guard-refused plan row is still reported by name in v_drops; the progress arm is not verified at all. Accepted to land only because §1 makes the old arm fire on every honest player and no ceremony is scheduled - NOT because the replacement is equivalent. BLOCKING FOLLOW-UP with a precise trigger: restore the counting shape (insert ... on conflict ... returning (xmax = 0), incrementing v_n_prog only on a real INSERT, compared against bootstrap_rows + v_n_prog) BEFORE any wipe-day ceremony, i.e. the moment hearthrise.import_reopen is set. v_n_prog stays the receipt's “rows imported” and is still reported. Special-casing trait:auto_eat in the counter and seeding a pre-plan baseline were both considered and rejected (the first goes stale on the next bootstrap-written row; the second over-counts, because the plan's on-conflict-do-update adds no row when it collides). This file does NOT become hr_import_apply's last author - it patches one statement and restates nothing; its ACL (callable by NO role) is captured before the replace and asserted byte-identical after. PATCHES hr_create_character PROGRAMMATICALLY at ONE guarded exactly-once anchor (its final success return), CR-TOLERANT - production stores that body with CRLF while the repo file is LF, measured - with proacl asserted unchanged (hr_create_character is authenticated-only and DELIBERATELY not hr_engine-executable: server-authority §2a-iv, the engine must never mint characters i.e. starting kits; §2 re-asserts all three). The grant goes AFTER the ledger row on purpose: the journal describes the KIT, and tests/character-bootstrap-guard.mjs compares that meta field-by-field against src/data/start-kit.js. NO CLIENT CHANGE IS NEEDED TO OWN IT: hr_state_of already projects the owned trait set and src/net/accrue.js reconcileTraits already unions it into G.traits, so Settings' ownsAutoEat(), the death sheet's autoEatOwned, the Bounty Shop's owned marker and HearthriseAuto's `owned` gate all light up unchanged. §grant-existing (behind its own GUC `hearthrise.grant_auto_eat_existing='yes'`, unset = skipped with a notice) grants the identical row to every EXISTING character with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING - trivial and idempotent, offered because every current beta player suffered the same loop. It grants the FLAG ONLY and deliberately does NOT enable auto-eat for them: hr_set_auto_eat reads auth.uid() and cannot be called for another user, and writing player_state.auto_eat_* for somebody else from a migration would make this file a writer of a live player's settings. ⚠⚠ WHO EATS AND WHO DEBITS - THIS NOTE HAS BEEN WRONG TWICE, and both retracted versions are quoted rather than deleted because a reader who saw an earlier draft needs to recognise what they read. RETRACTED #1 (original): “this file does not flip the CLIENT's live-combat switch (G.autoActions.eat.enabled, default false)” - FALSE for the population that matters. DEFAULTS.eat.enabled is false, but ensureShape() in src/features/auto-actions.js (the b163 branch) sets aa.eat.enabled = true whenever G.foodSlot is truthy, and the fresh-G literal carries foodSlot:'cooked_shrimp' - which THIS PROGRAM put there in b495. A fresh character is `owned + ON`. RETRACTED #2 (the first “correction”, and the one that fooled the review): “the server's sim only eats during AWAY accrual”, therefore “§1 IS SAFE ONLY IF THE ATTENDED-EAT GATE FIX SHIPS IN THE SAME BUILD” - ALSO FALSE, and an inference from the WORD “away” rather than a reading of the function. Acting on it would have been worse than leaving it alone: the Systems Engineer built the “fix” it demanded and MEASURED that it destroys items via a double debit (1090/1091). THE TRUE MODEL, read off source: computeAccrual has NO PRESENCE INPUT AT ALL - hr-accrue/accrual.js:1084 gates on `inp.autoEatEnabled === true` and nothing else, the eat is a real debit at ~line 1200 (`itemDelta[foodId] -= 1`), and src/net/accrue.js decideSettle returns {settle:false, reason:'hidden'} while the tab is hidden, so the 90 s settle loop (SETTLE_INTERVAL_MS = 90000) runs ONLY while visible and every settle it performs prices an ATTENDED window. With auto_eat_enabled=true the server therefore prices and DEBITS every attended meal at each visible settle; the client's pending-consume hold drains against the server's own movement instead of expiring, so there is no restock and no free food. clientOwnsAutoEatDebit() refusing to send is CORRECT - sending on top would debit the same meal twice, which is item LOSS. WHY §1 IS SAFE: not because of a gate fix (there is none and none was needed) but because the server OWNS and DEBITS the attended meals it enables. PINNED so the premise cannot be re-asserted a third time: branch fix/attended-eat-intent-gate (2087eba3, comment-only + two guards, merging in the SAME BUILD) adds attendedSettleAutoEatGuard in tests/accrual-engine.mjs and EAT-RESTOCK-6 block 2b in src/features/smoke-test.js, which turns RED if the client is ever made to send the intent while the server is eating. All four source claims were re-read here before this paragraph was written, not taken on report. The AWAY half is unaffected and is what the ruling actually buys. §0 fails closed without hr_set_auto_eat / hr_auto_eat_tier / hr_auto_eat_max_pct / hr_traits AND without the PAID upgrade still existing (auto_eat_2 present, cost > 0, req_trait = 'auto_eat', and max_pct(1) < max_pct(2)) - if the sink ever vanishes, making tier I free stops being “remove the entry tax” and becomes “give the feature away”. COST AT 100x PLAYERS: ONE player_progress row per CHARACTER (~80 bytes; ~0.3 MB at 3,500 characters) and ZERO new ledger rows - the switch is an UPDATE of the row the same block inserted. Journal rule 6 is about per-TICK logging; this is per-character and adds no journal row at all. REVERSIBLE: re-apply 2026-08-14-character-bootstrap.sql (restores hr_create_character) and 2026-08-17-cutover-import.sql (restores the progress verify). The delete of granted flags is in the file's header and carries TWO not-exists clauses (Security F6, 2026-08-30): the live player_ledger row (intent='trait_buy:auto_eat') AND its shadow in player_ledger_rollup (kind='trait'). The second is the fix - hr_ledger_prune deletes rows older than hr_ledger_config.retain_days (default 90) and rolls them up WITHOUT `intent`, so the first clause alone silently stops protecting every player who bought Auto-Eat more than ~90 days ago, and the row that proved they paid is exactly the row that is gone. The rollup discriminator is deliberately COARSE (any long-ago trait purchase spares the character), which over-protects - the correct direction when the other error is an undetectable revoke of something bought with Marks. A dedicated marker row was considered and rejected: a permanent row per character on every envelope, forever, to serve a manual operation that runs at most once, when the rollup is already prune-proof by construction. TESTS: tests/auto-eat-at-creation.mjs (PGlite, full replay: the trait lands, the tier reads 1, the switch is on at the derived clamp, version stays 0 and the journal stays ONE row, a cutover dry-run still imports, hr_trait_buy answers already_owned and charges nothing, the auto_eat_2 path is unchanged, ACLs and policies hold; plus A10, which EXTRACTS the documented rollback from the header and EXECUTES it against a granted character, a purchaser with a live ledger row and a purchaser whose row has been pruned into the rollup - a comment is not a control; 8 mutations, all caught, 5 of them with the migration's own §2 blinded so the guard alone must see them). Client half in the same commit: src/features/death-sheet.js (the tips now key on the SWITCH, not the entitlement - which matters for the player who turned it OFF, since a fresh character is `owned + ON`) + its smoke tests. SECURITY: NEW creation-time GRANT surface on hr_create_character + a one-statement patch to hr_import_apply - ACK REQUESTED. Direction of travel is a FREE convenience trait; no gold, gems, Marks, items or XP move. NOT auto-applied - REVIEW ONLY; the Coordinator applies.
